(“Acumen” or the “Company”) issued a press release regarding the topline results discussed in Item 8.01 of this Current Report on Form 8-K (this “Report”).

On October 30, 2026, the Company announced that, based on initial topline data from its Phase 2 ALTITUDE-AD clinical trial of sabirnetug (ACU193) in participants with early Alzheimer’s disease, the clinical trial did not meet its primary endpoint of change from baseline in cognitive and functional decline as measured by the Integrated Alzheimer’s Disease Rating Scale at 18 months compared to placebo at either the 35 mg/kg or the 50 mg/kg dose.
The initial topline data indicate that sabirnetug was generally well tolerated, with amyloid-related imaging abnormalities - edema (“ARIA-E”) observed in ~10% of sabirnetug-treated participants.

Based on the initial topline results, the Company plans to cease development of sabirnetug, including the open-label extension portion of the ALTITUDE-AD trial, and to evaluate its strategic options, including its Enhanced Brain Delivery™ (EBD ® ) program.

These statements are based upon the current beliefs and expectations of the Company’s management, and are subject to certain factors, risks and uncertainties, including the risk that additional data or further analyses from ALTITUDE-AD may differ from, or change the interpretation of, the topline results, and particularly those inherent in the process of discovering, developing and commercializing safe and effective human therapeutics.
